title: Why Didn't Hanuman Defeat Vali?
source: Valmiki Ramayana, Uttara Kanda 7.35-36 and Kishkindha Kanda 4.65-66 (Critical Edition)

captions.instagram:
Hanuman was so mighty, so why didn't he save Sugriva from Vali? In Valmiki's Ramayana (Critical Edition), Rama himself asks this of the sage Agastya (Uttara 7.35.11). Agastya's answer: as a fearless child, full of the gods' boons, Hanuman troubled the sages' hermitages, and the sages of the Bhrigu and Angiras lines cursed him: "the strength you lean on, you will not know it for a long time" (7.36.33). That is why he didn't act when Vali hounded Sugriva (7.36.39-40). In the Ramcharitmanas, Jambavan reminds him: "का चुप साधि रहेहु बलवाना". Both tellings are told with devotion.

Did you know Rama himself asked why Hanuman didn't stop Vali? 👇 Jai Shri Ram! Jai Hanuman!

📜 Source: Valmiki Ramayana, Uttara Kanda 7.35-36 and Kishkindha Kanda 4.65-66 (Critical Edition)

captions.youtube_description:
Hanuman was so mighty, so why didn't he save Sugriva from Vali? In Valmiki's Ramayana (Critical Edition), Rama himself asks this of the sage Agastya (Uttara 7.35.11). Agastya's answer: as a fearless child, full of the gods' boons, Hanuman troubled the sages' hermitages, and the sages of the Bhrigu and Angiras lines cursed him: "the strength you lean on, you will not know it for a long time" (7.36.33). That is why he didn't act when Vali hounded Sugriva (7.36.39-40). In the Ramcharitmanas, Jambavan reminds him: "का चुप साधि रहेहु बलवाना". Both tellings are told with devotion.

Did you know Rama himself asked why Hanuman didn't stop Vali? 👇 Jai Shri Ram! Jai Hanuman!

Source: Valmiki Ramayana, Uttara Kanda 7.35-36 and Kishkindha Kanda 4.65-66 (Critical Edition)
Verses:
• Rama asks Agastya why Hanuman, so mighty, did not burn Vali like a creeper when the feud with Sugriva arose — 7.35.2; 7.35.11
• With the gods' boons the child was full of strength and fearlessly troubled the sages' hermitages — 7.36.27-31
• Sages of the Bhrigu and Angiras lines cursed him: he would not know his strength for a long time; his vigour was taken and he became gentle — 7.36.32-34
• Because of the curse Hanuman did not know his strength when the Vali-Sugriva feud arose, even while Sugriva was being hounded — 7.36.39-40
• He learned grammar facing the sun, moving backwards from the rising to the setting mountain — 7.36.42
• Jambavan: in strength, wisdom, brilliance and courage you surpass all beings; why do you not know yourself? — 4.65.7
• Praised, Hanuman grew in size — 4.66.1
• Ramcharitmanas: 'कहइ रीछपति सुनु हनुमाना। का चुप साधि रहेहु बलवाना।।' (no curse given) — Ramcharitmanas, Kishkindha Kand, after doha 29
